description: Single source of truth for all numeric quality gates (self-review, rewrite limits, paragraph/unit word bounds, style-fingerprint compliance, voice rule-coverage/corpus minimums, typography). Edit here; every skill and agent references this file. Gemini model/thinking-budget defaults and retry policy are NOT read from here — they live in SPEC_DEFAULTS in plugins/academic-writer/mcp/gemini-server/src/gemini-client.ts (overridable per-project via profile.md), and the retry constants are hardcoded in that same file. The antiAi block was REMOVED in 0.9.0: nothing computed that score, so it was the drafting model rating its own unrevised draft, and it measured a flat maximum on every paragraph of a live 13-unit run while the auditor failed several of the same paragraphs. Anti-AI patterns are now writing guidance (write/references/anti-ai-patterns-*.md), not a scored gate; the auditor's VERDICT is the per-paragraph gate.

selfReview._comment: Articles scoring below 40/60 trigger researcher review before final output. 6 dimensions x 10 points each.

rewriteCycles._comment: Maximum number of times a paragraph can be rewritten before being included with [NEEDS REVIEW].

paragraph._comment: Soft word ceiling per paragraph. Introduction and conclusion paragraphs may exceed by wordCeilingIntroConclusionBonus words. wordFloor: minimum words for one drafted paragraph. The drafted-unit word gate is per planned paragraph (n x [wordFloor, wordCeiling]); writerUnit min/max bound the ARCHITECT's unit sizing, not a single draft (live run 2026-09-23: a 1-paragraph unit correctly drafted ~110 words failed a 300-word unit floor). quotedTermMaxWords: a quoted span of at most this many words is treated as a term (scare quotes, e.g. ״יש מאין״), not a source quotation, by the draft quote gate.

writerUnit._comment: Min/target/max word bounds for a 'writer unit' — the leaf-level chunk that gets exactly one section-writer subagent. Sections whose word count exceeds maxWords must be decomposed by the architect into multiple writer-unit subsections (an outline `units` array); adjacent subsections under minWords should be merged into one unit rather than left tiny.

write._comment: Architect may label up to this many thesis alternatives for discussion; none replaces author intent unless the author edits it.

styleFingerprint._comment: Per-dimension style compliance score. Below 7 triggers paragraph adjustment.

exemplars._comment: src/scripts/extract-voice-exemplars.py: how many real paragraphs from past-articles/ are shown to Gemini as few-shot voice examples, their word bounds, and at most maxPerFile per source article so no single paper dominates the voice. Measured 2026-09-15 on the author's finished Hebrew papers: mean paragraph 97-134 words, so 40-150 keeps typical body paragraphs and drops headings and footnote-length fragments (a whole-folder corpus reads shorter because course reflections pull the mean down). Gemini guidance: 2-5 examples; more rarely helps.

proofread._comment: Proofread chunk target; execution and call budgets are configured under models and budget.

ocr._comment: Ported from the retired MCP gemini_ocr tool (PER_CALL_PAGE_CAP, GEMINI_BATCH_SIZE, INLINE_SIZE_LIMIT_BYTES = 20*1024*1024). perCallPageCap bounds how many pages one `aw ocr` invocation processes before truncating (Files API upload path for pages over inlineSizeLimitBytes was not ported to the CLI -- see T15a handoff notes; oversized pages fail with a named ERROR instead of silently uploading). geminiBatchSize is 1 (the bake-off measured one page per call; the 2026-10-16 six-page batches dropped passages) and lowResDpi is 100 from the 2026-10-20 OCR bake-off: below 100 dpi Gemini read Hebrew more accurately than Claude, so the Claude and local tiers flag those pages. claudeModel is the Claude reader (Opus: Sonnet 5.5 tied it but twice answered a book page with a summary instead of the text, and Haiku 5.5 was 1.4 points worse on poor scans). Round 3 of the bake-off set the auto order, page by page: a free reading is kept when Surya and Tesseract agree at freeAgreeMin (letters-only similarity; 17 of 54 test pages passed, Surya median 0.3% letter error on them against 0.13% for Gemini and 0.0% for Opus, worst 1.1%), then Claude, then Gemini. A Claude answer whose letters are under shortAnswerRatio of Tesseract's reading goes to Gemini: every real Claude answer was at least 0.9 of it and every soft refusal under 0.35. Pages whose Tesseract reading has under shortAnswerMinChars letters skip that check.

citationFloor._comment: VER-18 absence gate, enforced by src/scripts/gate.py citation-floor. The per-paragraph auditor is a PRESENCE check — it verifies that claims which ARE cited are cited correctly, and is structurally blind to a paragraph that cites nothing. Absence needs its own counting gate, and the count is arithmetic, not judgement (TST-02). Only SECONDARY citations count toward the floor: primary sources stay inline in this field, so a raw citation count reads healthy on an article carrying almost no scholarly engagement. minSecondaryPer1000Words is the rate floor, minSecondaryTotal the absolute floor that keeps a very short article from passing on rate alone. The gate FAILS if EITHER floor is breached.

typography._comment: dashReplacement is the default em/en-dash fix convention used by detect-ai-typography.py (values: hyphen|comma|colon|remove); overridable via --dash-replacement. topFrequentTermsCount/minTermLength configure extract-style-metrics.py's frequentTerms extraction. furnitureMaxWords/furnitureShare/furnitureMinCount drop structural furniture (table-of-contents lines and section headers) from frequentTerms: a term is furniture when at least furnitureShare of its occurrences fall in paragraphs of at most furnitureMaxWords words and it occurs at least furnitureMinCount times. Calibrated on a real 10-file corpus of 857 paragraphs with a 38-word median: the author's own name sits in 5-word ToC lines and scores 96%, subject vocabulary scores 3%, and the highest-scoring term that is kept scores 73% — so the 0.8 cutoff has margin on both sides. Only terms in contention for the reported list are judged — the top topFrequentTermsCount * furnitureCandidateMultiplier by raw count — because a share computed over a handful of occurrences has no resolution: ב׳ and א׳, the same token doing the same job in the same two files, scored 0.80 and 0.50 on five and seven observations and split. Replaces a front-matter rule that inspected the first N paragraphs of each file and never fired, because these headers repeat throughout a document rather than opening it.

proofread._comment: Token ceiling comfortably covers a long proofread run; the USD ceiling is the primary cost guard.

write._comment: Token ceiling covers multi-section drafting; the USD ceiling is the primary cost guard.

voiceMoves._comment: One call to derive qualitative voice moves.

revise._comment: One bounded classification pass for author review items.

awImprove._comment: Development-only defect clustering and Jev roster thresholds.

_piModelNote: piModel = OpenRouter model for the isolated Pi judge. Must be a non-Claude, non-Gemini family (cross-family verification); taken from the author's Pi model roster (executor tier, machine-config/pi/model-roster.json). Runs in shadow until the Hebrew fixture shows parity.

evidence._comment: aw evidence build coverage targets per source. Live rehearsal 2026-09-23: with no target, Gemini returned 5 passages for a 12-page core text and 0 for Sefer Yetzirah, missing the article's opening dilemma. The core text (author-intent coreTextSourceId) gets dense coverage; every other source a smaller floor. Concurrency for evidence.extract is 4 (sources in parallel).

synthesis._comment: aw synthesize: a paragraph opener (first openerWords words) used at least repeatedOpenerMin times across the article is passed to the synthesizer as a required variation (live rehearsal 2026-09-23: 7 units opened with the same phrase, 0 edits proposed).

activity._comment: A run counts as active (hooks append to it, the reader shows it as running) while its activity.jsonl has a run_start, no run_end and was written within this many minutes; older, it reads as stalled.

tokens._comment: Rough token estimate for the retrieval ledger: characters divided by this (Hebrew text packs about 2 characters per token, other scripts about 4). An estimate for comparing routes, never a billing figure.

index._comment: aw library index (PageIndex tree build): summaryModel is the LiteLLM model for page summaries, maxCalls the hard cap on model calls per run, concurrency the parallel calls, askAboveCalls the estimated call count above which the skill asks the researcher before starting (with a cost estimate) and the call cap a run without --yes gets, timeoutMs bounds one whole indexing run (30 minutes). verifyPages is how many pages the read-back compares with Trove, minSummaryShare the share of nodes that must carry a summary when summaries were asked for, probeTimeoutMs bounds the up-front check that the command can index at all.

install._comment: aw library install: pageindexCommit is the pinned PageIndex commit (its tarball sha256 lives in PINNED.json), minPython the least Python for the structure tier, minPythonCore the least for the core tier (index from the table of contents), pipTimeoutMs bounds one pip install (15 minutes), venvTimeoutMs the creation of the private Python folder, healthTimeoutMs the check after the install, probeTimeoutMs asking one Python what version it is. approxSizeMb is the rough disk size quoted to the researcher before an install (an estimate, not a measurement).

eval._comment: aw library eval (blind comparison of Trove and PageIndex): runTimeoutMs bounds one locate run, minClaimWords is the shortest sentence taken as a claim, maxAnswerPages the most pages one answer may name, perSourceShare the most sampled claims per cited source. maxClaims is the most claims sampled from an article, minPairs the fewest judged pairs before a verdict is shown, maxTurns, maxBudgetUsdPerRun, maxPagesPerRead and maxReads bound one locate run, parallel the runs at once, locateModel the model that locates a quote, expectedUsdPerRun the figure quoted to the researcher before running.

library._comment: aw library: one adapter in front of the Trove and PageIndex routes. timeoutMs.primary bounds each page-range lookup on the answering route, timeoutMs.readAll bounds a whole-book read (evidence builds, read all, get; a book of about 1,000 pages over a remote command) and timeoutMs.check each call of status --check. maxBufferBytes caps one command's output (a whole book). maxRequestPages caps one requested page list. maxPageNumber is the highest page number a request may name. pageindex.readChunkPages is pilib's per-call read cap, used only when pilib has no read --json; chunkConcurrency runs those chunks in parallel; metaScanMax is the most shelf books looked up one by one to find a Trove id (more than that needs an explicit shelf map). Retrieval ledger and shadow: timeoutMs.shadow bounds the quiet second lookup (the detached worker) and timeoutMs.verdictSettle is how long aw library verdict waits for a still-running shadow before it records shadow_pending. shadow.ops are the lookups that get a shadow; shadow.maxConcurrent caps live workers per project (more are skipped as busy); shadow.readAllMaxPages is the most pages one read may have and still be shadowed; shadow.lockStaleMs drops a worker slot nobody released and shadow.reapGraceMs is how long a slot must be idle before a dead holder's slot is taken over; shadow.pollMs is the file poll step. spool.maxBytes caps one spooled page set and spool.ttlHours deletes spool files. ledger.maxRowBytes, maxErrorChars and maxAgreePages keep each retrieval.jsonl row small. agree.jaccardMin is the word overlap at which two routes count as returning the same page; supports.tokenCoverageMin is the share of the auditor quote's words that must appear in the shadow page text, and minQuoteTokens the shortest quote that is tested. report.minLookups is the fewest lookups per route before the report stops calling its rates rough.
